Question: In the US, when you have jury duty, does it count as a vacation day to your employer or how does that work?
Answer: It depends on the employer. When I last had jury duty (the only time I’ve had it) my employer was Verizon. Verizon’s policy at that time was to pay the employee for time missed for jury duty as if you had worked that day. They did not take it from any of the paid time off options such as vacation, sick time, holidays etc. I was appreciative of my employer for this policy because it was not mandated by law that they do this. Question: If Bill Russell has eleven championships and Jordan has six, why is Jordan considered the goat?
Answer: If Bill Russell has eleven championships and Jordan has six, why is Jordan considered the goat? Well first of all, the GOAT is determined not just by how many rings you won, but by many other criteria such as regular season and playoff base and advanced stats, MVPs, All-NBA and All-Defense awards, DPOY, great basketball moments, etc. And if we’re going to talk rings, we need to talk about how you won the rings. If you look up players who have won the most rings, you’ll find Bill Russell alone at #1 with 11 rings, Same Jones at #2 with 10 rings, and then 4 players tied at #3 with 8 rings: Tom Heinshon, KC Jones, John Havlicek, and Satch Sanders. All the aforementioned players played for and won championships with the Boston Celtics. All of them were on the same championship teams with each other and all are in the Hall of Fame. So who gets credit for the championships when more than one player plays on a championship team? The best player, right? And how do you determine the best player? There are almost as many ways as people if not more. Now I came up with a way to determine the unquestioned best player on a championship team that works with stats available since the 1951–1952 season. So it’s fairly era-agnostic, though far from perfect in this regard. So I detail my measuring criteria in my answer here: I use PER, WS, WS/48 in both the regular season and the playoffs with some minimal eligibility requirements to compare and see who was the leader in all 3 stats in the regular season and in the playoffs for a championship team. Now, unsurprisingly, many champions don’t have a player that comes out as the best in all 6 stats. So who came out the most in all 6 stats? Michael Jordan was the leader 6 out of 6 championships. Magic Johnson and Lebron James accomplished this 3 times each to tie for 2nd place. Bill Russell and several others did it 2 times each to tie for 4th place all-time. So Jordan led his team in PER, WS, WS/48 in both playoffs and in regular season for all 6 championships. Russell led his team in PER, WS, WS/48 in both playoffs and in regular season for 2 of his 11 championships. Now, Jordan also led the NBA in scoring for all 6 championships while winning the regular season scoring title, being nominated to 1st team All-NBA, 1st team All-Defense, and winning the Finals MVP. 5 of those championships Jordan led the NBA in WS, OWS, WS/48, OBPM, BPM, and VORP in the regular season (not sure about playoffs). 3 of those championships Jordan led the NBA in PER, OWS, WS, WS/48, OBPM, BPM, and VORP. I hope that you can now see SOME of the reasons why so many consider Michael Jordan the GOAT instead of Bill Russell despite Russell having 5 more championships than Jordan did. There are many more factors that support Jordan over Russell and others, but I’m going to stop here. Now lest some think that Bill Russell was some chump, he most definitely was not. Russell is one of the greatest players ever to play in the NBA. He was a pioneer in NBA and we may not have it today without his efforts in the 50’s and 60’s. He was great. Jordan just appears to be a little more greater in NBA basketball.

Question: Why do some people believe that Lebron is a better basketball player than Michael Jordan, even though he has not won an NBA championship without having two other strong players on his team?
Answer: Why do some people believe that Lebron is a better basketball player than Michael Jordan, even though he has not won an NBA championship without having two other strong players on his team? 1st of all, I don’t think any team has won a championship without at least 3 strong players. Strong in this context is a mighty ambiguous word and I would hate to use it against Lebron or any player. Usually in this context All-Star is used instead of strong. Now Lebron won 2 of his championships in 2012 and 2013 with 2 other All-Stars on his team besides himself. He won another with just 1 All-Star other than himself in 2020. Finally, Lebron in 2016 when he was the only All-Star on the team. Compare the above to Michael Jordan who won 4 championships with just Pippen as the only All-Star besides MJ on his team in 1992,1993, 1996, and 1997. Jordan won 2 championships in 1991 and 1998 where he was the only All-Star on his team. Just looking at this again, to me it doesn’t seem like Lebron was the clearcut best player on his 2020 championship team. He and Anthony Davis are pretty neck-and-neck in both the regular season and the playoffs. Lebron has a decent lead in assists in both but AD was 1st team All-Defense. Is it Lebron’s fault that AD was just as good as him that year? No, it’s not. That doesn’t in anyway take away that championship, but Jordan has 3 more championships where MJ was the clearcut best player on his team in the regular season and the Playoffs. That Lebron has 2 less rings than MJ and 3 less where LBJ is the clearcut best player is not a conclusive or main argument that Jordan is more “deserving” of the status of GOAT than Lebron. However, it should be a contributing part of the argument in favor of Jordan. So this is a small point for Jordan. That’s OK he has plenty more. Likewise, longer longevity should not be a conclusive or even main argument that Lebron is more “deserving” of the title of GOAT than MJ. However, it should be a contributing part of the argument in favor of Lebron. So longevity is a small point for Lebron. I would argue though that it should be slightly, but only very slightly less weighted than Championships. The goal of the GOAT should be primarily to do the utmost to help his team win games and the championship. That’s why they play the game to win. You don’t play to see who can play the longest. Now when you look at the totality of the package each Lebron and Jordan bring to the table for being the GOAT and helping his team win games and championships, it becomes clear to me that Lebron is not on MJ’s level. Here’s a little sample of what I’m talking about below: Jordan led his team to more championships than anyone else as the clearcut best player on his team. MJ was the best scorer in NBA history. Jordan was the best two-way player in NBA history.

Question: How long can LeBron James maintain his MVP status in the NBA if he continues to win finals with less talented teammates compared to other players who have never won titles?
Answer: How long can LeBron James maintain his MVP status in the NBA if he continues to win finals with less talented teammates compared to other players who have never won titles? Lebron hasn’t had the MVP in a long time. He won his last MVP back in 2012–2013, 11 years ago. He’s been a top 5 contender since then several times. However since 2017–2018, 7 years ago, he’s only been top 5 in the Bubble year which makes it a little iffy to many people including me. The Bubble gave him months of extra rest and he still only played 67 out of 71 of his teams games. He played in only 55 games the previous season and only 45 the following season. He did lead the NBA in assists but his assist-to-turnover ratio wasn’t stellar, especially for the the latest era. Other than assists, it didn’t appear to be one of Lebron’s better years IMO. Sure I would love to be able to average half the points, assists, and rebounds that he did in the NBA. Heck, I’d love just to be able to earn the end of the bench honors in the NBA. So having “MVP status” is a thing of the past for Lebron and is very unlikely to return. He was in strong contention or winning (4 MVPs) for a long time. He was no less than top 5 in voting for 13 straight years and did it an additional 2 years for a total of 15 years altogether which is a HUGE accomplishment. As for winning titles, Lebron has only won 1 title, the Bubble year, since his historic 2015–2016 upset of the 73–10 Golden State Warriors to win the NBA championship. Since the 2019–2020 Bubble year title, the closest that Lebron has gotten to going back to the Finals is a 4–0 sweep in last year’s WCF by the Nuggets. Lebron has NOT won the championship with some highly talented teams, so comparing him to other players who never won with “less” talent” is going to be a very small pool if you count the highest talent that Lebron had and didn’t win the Finals. Instead of focusing on these iffy comparisons, why not celebrate Lebron for all the great things that he has done? 4 Championships, 4 MVPs, 4 Finals MVPs, 15 years as a top 5 player, 40K points scored, 21 seasons played, etc. And I know of very very few people who would rank any player who didn’t win at least one title ahead of Lebron in all-time rankings.
